questions.question: What property must a solid material have to allow liquid particles to diffuse through it?
options: It must be impermeable
It must be permeable
It must be completely solid without any spaces
It must be magnetized

questions.question: When observing a colored liquid diffusing into a clear jelly cube, what would you expect to see over time?
options: The color remains only on the very outer surface of the cube
The color spreads from the outside toward the center of the cube
The cube turns completely color-free as the liquid is repelled
The cube instantly dissolves and disappears

questions.question: If you increase the temperature of the liquid surrounding a jelly cube, how does this affect the rate of diffusion into the cube?
options: Diffusion slows down because particles lose energy
Diffusion stops completely because the jelly melts
Diffusion speeds up because the particles have more kinetic energy
Temperature has no effect on the rate of diffusion

questions.question: If you compare a large jelly cube with a small jelly cube, which one will have its center reached by a diffusing liquid first?
options: The large cube, because it has more surface area
The small cube, because the liquid has a shorter distance to travel to the center
Both cubes at the exact same time
Neither, as diffusion only occurs on the surface of any object

questions.question: Which particle-based explanation best describes why diffusion happens faster at higher temperatures in a jelly cube?
options: Particles move slower and clump together
Particles gain kinetic energy, move faster, and collide more frequently
The jelly particles expand and block the diffusing liquid
The liquid particles shrink in size at higher temperatures

questions.question: Why can only certain substances diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: Only magnetic substances can pass through
Their particles are small enough to fit through the tiny holes in the membrane
The membrane has active pumps that grab only large particles
Only gas particles can ever pass through a membrane

questions.question: When particles diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane, in which direction do they move?
options: They only move from the inside to the outside
They only move from the outside to the inside
They move through the membrane in both directions
They stop moving once they hit the membrane

questions.question: If there is a high concentration of glucose particles outside a selectively-permeable membrane and a low concentration inside, what is the predicted net movement of glucose?
options: Net movement of glucose into the membrane
Net movement of glucose out of the membrane
No net movement of glucose in either direction
Glucose particles will stick to the membrane and not enter

questions.question: In an experiment using Visking tubing filled with starch solution placed in a beaker of water, why does starch not diffuse out into the water?
options: Water molecules block the starch from leaving
Starch particles are too large to pass through the pores of the Visking tubing
The temperature of the water is too low for starch to move
Starch is attracted to the inner surface of the tubing and cannot leave

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding cell cytoplasm and the substances dissolved within it?
options: They are continuous liquids with no individual particles
They are made up of tiny particles that are constantly in motion
They consist only of empty space with no particles
They are solid blocks that cannot move

questions.question: How do essential substances like oxygen enter a cell through the cell membrane?
options: They are pushed through by the cell's muscles
They diffuse through tiny holes in the cell membrane
They dissolve the cell membrane to create large openings
They are converted into energy before passing through

questions.question: Why are some large molecules, such as proteins, unable to diffuse into a cell?
options: They are repelled by the electrical charge of the cell membrane
They are too big to fit through the holes in the cell membrane
They travel too fast to be caught by the membrane
They are only found in solid form and cannot diffuse

questions.question: What makes a cell membrane selectively-permeable?
options: It allows all substances to pass through freely
It blocks all substances from entering or leaving the cell
It only allows certain substances to diffuse through it based on properties like particle size
It only lets water in but never lets anything out

questions.question: How do particles in a liquid or gas move during diffusion?
options: In straight, organized lines directly to their destination
In random directions, colliding with each other all the time
Only in a downward direction due to gravity
They remain completely still and do not move

questions.question: What is the definition of concentration in the context of liquids or gases?
options: The total weight of the container holding the substance
The number of particles in a specific volume of liquid or gas
The speed at which particles are moving
The temperature of the liquid or gas

questions.question: What is meant by particles moving down a concentration gradient?
options: Moving from an area of lower concentration to an area of higher concentration
Moving from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration
Moving upwards against gravity
Moving only when heat is applied to the system

questions.question: Which of the following best defines diffusion?
options: The active pumping of particles from low to high concentration requiring energy
The passive movement of particles from an area of higher to lower concentration
The chemical reaction between two different liquids
The settling of solid particles at the bottom of a container
